title: Storage & disks
blurb: Disk full, external drives, USB sticks, disk errors.

remedies.title: "System Data" takes up a huge part of my Mac's storage
remedies.why: System Data includes caches, logs, Time Machine local snapshots and app support files.

steps.text: Restart the Mac; temporary files and local snapshots shrink by themselves.
Clean caches and logs with DeskMedic's Cleanup.
Find big folders in the Disk map (Library, Xcode, iOS backups, Docker).
Old iPhone backups: System Settings › General › Storage › iOS Files.

remedies.title: Windows folder takes a lot of space (WinSxS, old updates)
remedies.why: Windows keeps components and the previous version (Windows.old) for 10 days to allow going back.

steps.text: DeskMedic's Cleanup includes old Windows update files.
Disk Cleanup › Clean up system files › Windows Update Cleanup and Previous Windows installation(s).
Don't delete WinSxS files by hand; Windows needs them.

remedies.title: A drive or partition has no letter, or the D: drive vanished
remedies.why: Windows lost the letter, or a new disk was never set up (initialised and formatted).

steps.text: Look in DeskMedic's Disks page for the drive and its state.
Disk Management: right-click the volume › Change Drive Letter and Paths › Add.
A brand-new empty disk shows as "Not initialized": initialise it (GPT) and create a volume. Don't do this on a disk that has data.

remedies.title: Check my disk's health
remedies.why: Drives report their own health; warnings mean back up and replace soon.

steps.text: DeskMedic's Health check and Disks page show health and warnings.
Settings › System › Storage › Advanced storage settings › Disks & volumes › Properties shows Drive health.
Disk Utility shows S.M.A.R.T. status for the drive; System Information › Storage too.

remedies.title: Encrypt a USB stick or external drive
remedies.why: An encrypted drive keeps files safe if it's lost.

steps.text: Right-click the drive › Turn on BitLocker (Pro editions) and set a password; save the recovery key.
Disk Utility › Erase with an encrypted format (APFS Encrypted), or right-click in Finder › Encrypt.
Encrypted drives may only open on the same kind of system.

remedies.title: Can't reach my home NAS or shared drive
remedies.why: The NAS changed address, is asleep, or the saved login is old.

steps.text: Open it by address: \\192.168.x.x in File Explorer (Windows) or smb://192.168.x.x with ⌘K (Mac).
Find its address in the router or the NAS maker's finder app.
Update the saved login.
Give the NAS a reserved address in the router.
